questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Choose suitable field types and identifiers and explain how validation protects data quality.
questions.prompt: A school stores contact numbers as whole numbers. Several local numbers lose their initial zero when saved. Recommend a field type and one separate validation rule for the school’s policy of accepting only 11 digits.
questions.answer: Use a text field. Require exactly 11 characters, each a digit.
questions.explanation: The value is an identifier and does not need arithmetic. Text preserves leading zeros. A length and character check enforces the stated local format.

markingGuide.description: Specify both length and digit constraints.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Choose suitable field types and identifiers and explain how validation protects data quality.
questions.prompt: A tool-hire shop wants to identify each customer record by surname or by an assigned customer code. Different customers can share a surname, and surnames can change. Recommend a key and explain how to keep it reliable.
questions.answer: Use the assigned customer code as a primary key. Require a non-empty, unique code and keep it stable.
questions.explanation: Uniqueness prevents two customers from sharing a record identifier. Stability means a name change need not affect references to the record.

markingGuide.description: State how to enforce uniqueness and preserve stability.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Choose suitable field types and identifiers and explain how validation protects data quality.
questions.prompt: A reading room needs to keep a record of each loan, including repeated borrowing of the same copy by the same pupil. Propose a primary key and three other fields that let staff identify the copy, the pupil and the day it went out. Explain why the copy code alone cannot be the key.
questions.answer: Use a unique LoanID as key, with CopyID, PupilID and LoanDate as separate fields.
questions.explanation: A copy may appear on many loan rows. Giving each transaction its own identifier preserves repeat loans without confusing a loan with the item loaned.

markingGuide.description: Include separate copy and pupil identifiers.
Explain why a copy code repeats across rows.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Choose suitable field types and identifiers and explain how validation protects data quality.
questions.prompt: In a table where each row represents one school bus trip, what is one record?
questions.answer: All the stored field values for one trip.
questions.explanation: A row represents one occurrence. Each column holds a field such as the trip date or the vehicle code.
options: A column containing the dates of all trips.
All the stored field values for one trip.
A single field name at the top of a column.
The list of data types used in the table.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Choose suitable field types and identifiers and explain how validation protects data quality.
questions.prompt: A school database has a numeric field for hours spent on a task. The agreed rule allows values from 0 to 8 inclusive. Which input will a correct range check reject?
questions.explanation: The value 8.5 exceeds the upper bound. Both endpoints and intermediate values satisfy the rule.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Select records using criteria and distinguish data entry, retrieval and presentation functions.
questions.prompt: A library’s overdue list includes returned books because the query checks only whether DueDate is before today. Give a corrected rule using the Yes/No field Returned. Explain why a book due today is excluded.
questions.answer: Use DueDate < Today AND Returned = No. A book due today fails the strict earlier-than condition.
questions.explanation: Both tests must be true. The date identifies overdue loans, and the status removes returned copies.

markingGuide.description: Explain why a due date equal to today does not qualify.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Select records using criteria and distinguish data entry, retrieval and presentation functions.
questions.prompt: A bursar’s query produces the correct unpaid entries. The bursar needs a printable summary grouped by class with a subtotal per class. Describe how the query and the report should work together.
questions.answer: Use the unpaid query as the source for a report. Group the report by class and sum the outstanding amount for each group.
questions.explanation: The query selects relevant records. The report arranges those records for reading and adds class totals without changing the underlying balances.

markingGuide.description: Use the unpaid query as the report source.
Group by class and specify the amount to subtotal.
Distinguish the selection and presentation roles.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Select records using criteria and distinguish data entry, retrieval and presentation functions.
questions.prompt: A repairs database must show all jobs that are either awaiting a part or assigned urgent priority. Which criterion includes a job satisfying either condition, including jobs satisfying both?
questions.answer: Status = Awaiting part OR Priority = Urgent
questions.explanation: OR is inclusive here. A row is retained whenever at least one of the two conditions is true.
options: Status = Awaiting part AND Priority = Urgent
Status = Awaiting part AND Priority is not Urgent
Status = Awaiting part OR Priority = Urgent
Status is not Awaiting part OR Priority is not Urgent

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Select records using criteria and distinguish data entry, retrieval and presentation functions.
questions.prompt: A cooperative’s clerk needs a screen for entering one member’s details at a time. Which database object is specifically designed to provide that kind of data-entry interface?
questions.explanation: A form can arrange data-entry controls for one record and save values into the underlying data source.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.learningObjective: Select records using criteria and distinguish data entry, retrieval and presentation functions.
questions.prompt: A query selects Stock < ReorderPoint. Item P has stock 12 and reorder point 12. Item Q has 7 and 9. Item R has 8 and 6. Which items appear?
questions.explanation: P fails because equality is excluded. Q is below its own reorder point. R is above its reorder point.
